doc.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Bird, Coltrane and Dinah Washington recollections
title: Recording with Dinah: Quincy Jones, Hal Mooney and Bobby Shad
summary: Cobb recalls Quincy Jones's arrangements for For Those in Love and the Capitol producer Bobby Shad.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Another thing that interests me is – or I think would be of interest – is, during Dinah’s time, you did recordings with people like Hal Mooney and his orchestra, and then you did things with Quincy Jones. I think there probably was a big difference.

The thing with Quincy Jones was an album called For Those in Love, I think. That was maybe one of the first arrangements that Quincy had ever done like that, plus it was at the beginning of his career too, when that was happening. But they were friends, and so he did it, because they were friends, and we were friends.
Did she push him forward in that circumstance?

I don’t think she – she probably – that probably helped him, because he arranged the music for that date. He probably got some note from that, I’m sure. I’m sure – like I say, I’m sure it helped him, one way or another.
From the standpoint of the music that was happening in the orchestrations, was there really a marked difference between the kind of things that Hal Mooney was putting forward and . . . ?
Yeah, this is before Hal Mooney. Hal Mooney’s much later.
That was great. They were friends too. I think the record company – what was it? What was the record company? Capitol?
They met, and he liked the way she sang. So they got together and made some things. I’m trying to think if it was Bobby Shad or who it was that hooked all this – was the . . .
A&R [artists and repertory] guy at the time?

Yeah. I remember one record date we did, Bobby Shad was there, was the A&R guy. I mean, he produced and all like that. So this might be one of those. He did a few of those. He wrote nice arrangements for her. They were a perfect pair.
